chapter: MJQ, Pettiford and the move to Paris
title: Playing with Oscar Pettiford at Cafe Bohemia; the Savoy contract
summary: After leaving the MJQ he joined Oscar Pettiford at the Cafe Bohemia, a job Allen Eager got them, and had a Savoy contract letting him record when he found something interesting.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: And after I left the Modern Jazz Quartet, I began to play with Oscar, Oscar Pettiford.
Oh, I see, yes.
So we started at the [Cafe] Bohemia.
Oh, yeah, he was wonderful. Duke loved him so dearly.
That was the man. And we played -- we stayed there at the --
He was a classicist too, wasn't he?
Oh, he was something else, something else. And we played the Bohemia with Allen Eager.
Yeah.
Allen Eager was a good friend of the owner.
Oh.
So Allen got us the job, Oscar and I.
Yeah.

He said, 'Come on, man. This guy has a striptease show in his place and I've talked him into bringing in jazz, so I'd like for you and Klook to come over and start out with me.' So we did. Duke Jordan, Oscar and myself.
Yeah.
So after awhile, Allen, he you know, he's crazy about horses and he's always marrying rich women.
Yeah.
So he just left. He said, 'Okay, you guys, you've got it,' you know.
Yeah.
[Adderley] So then, that's when we introduced Cannonball and all those guys, because I had like a contract with Savoy.
With the record company.
The record company.
Yeah.
And Lubinsky told me, "You can make records, any time you find something interesting, you just tell me the day before, and we'll record the next day."
Yeah.
